description: Registry of known prior clinical and scientific beliefs to check against AI evidence in Agent 4E. Each entry defines a belief, its domain, and the signal that would constitute disproof.

assumption_types.Region_Irrelevance: AI analysis (Grad-CAM, attention, SHAP) assigns zero or negligible weight to a region previously assumed important
assumption_types.Mechanism_Misattribution: AI evidence shows a symptom or biomarker traces to a different anatomical source than assumed
assumption_types.Predictor_Surprise: A variable assumed irrelevant achieves top predictive rank; a variable assumed dominant drops out
assumption_types.Biomarker_Sequence_Reversal: AI evidence shows a biomarker signal appears earlier than previously assumed in the disease cascade
assumption_types.Feature_Insufficient: A feature assumed sufficient as a standalone biomarker fails when tested in isolation
assumption_types.Feature_Context_Dependent: A feature assumed universally effective fails in one context but succeeds in another

known_assumptions.belief: The optic nerve head (ONH) is a key retinal biomarker for MCI via the brain-eye connection
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Multiple retinal MCI papers, 2018-2022
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: XAI analysis (Grad-CAM, attention) assigns zero or negligible weight to ONH region in a retinal MCI classification model
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: Retinal MCI biomarkers reside in RNFL thinning and vascular morphology, not the optic disc. OCT analysis should focus on parafoveal RNFL.

known_assumptions.belief: In CHF patients, cardiac-specific features (ejection fraction, cardiac output) dominate MCI risk
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Clinical cardiology-neurology literature, 2015-2020
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: ML feature importance ranking places cardiac output features outside top predictors; psychosocial or metabolic features rank higher
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: CHF-MCI screening should prioritise psychosocial adaptation and thyroid function assessments over cardiac function metrics.

known_assumptions.belief: Postcentral gyrus voxel-mirrored homotopic connectivity (VMHC) is a reliable standalone MCI biomarker
known_assumptions.assumed_since: VMHC MCI literature, 2016-2021
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: SVM using postcentral-gyrus VMHC alone achieves near-chance accuracy (below 70%) for binary MCI classification
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: Single-region interhemispheric connectivity markers are insufficient standalone. Multi-feature combination or DTI assessment of the same zone required.

known_assumptions.belief: Fine motor inconsistency in MCI patients reflects motor cortex or cerebellar atrophy
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Motor-cognition literature, 2010-2019
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: CART or equivalent analysis identifies hippocampal volume (not motor cortex volume) as primary predictor of trial-to-trial motor variability
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: Repeated-trial motor variability is a hippocampal-memory biomarker, not a motor biomarker. Motor variability testing can proxy medial temporal integrity without neuroimaging.

known_assumptions.belief: Posterior brain regions are the primary cognitive processing centres; their decline maps directly to cognitive impairment
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Posterior Cortical Atrophy literature; classical cognitive neuroscience
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: EEG attention mapping or saliency analysis finds frontal regions more active in cognitively declining patients than healthy controls, consistent with PASA (posterior-to-anterior shift in aging)
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: Elevated frontal EEG activity in MCI is a compensatory overactivation marker of posterior failure, not preserved frontal cognition. Frontal EEG hyperactivity should be interpreted as burden-displacement.

known_assumptions.belief: Corpus callosum volumetric loss is the earliest detectable white matter MCI signal
known_assumptions.assumed_since: White matter MCI literature, 2012-2020
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: Shape analysis (Fourier, surface irregularity) detects corpus callosum boundary changes that correlate with CSF p-tau before volumetric loss is measurable
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: Shape irregularity metrics should precede volumetric metrics in white matter staging models. Standard FreeSurfer volume-only pipelines miss an earlier signal.

known_assumptions.belief: Gyral surface connectivity features are effective primary MCI discriminators
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Cortical surface analysis MCI literature, 2015-2021
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: A gyral-zone surface connectivity feature achieves near-chance accuracy as a standalone feature, while DTI tract integrity through the same anatomical zone achieves AUC above 0.75
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: The functional unit is the white matter tract, not the cortical surface. Gyral zone features should be assessed via DTI fibre tract integrity, not surface VMHC.

known_assumptions.belief: Brain scans are categorically superior to cognitive and neuropsychological assessments for MCI conversion prediction
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Neuroimaging-dominant MCI literature consensus, widespread
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: Cognitive scores alone achieve higher AUC or accuracy than brain imaging alone for pMCI/sMCI conversion in a direct comparison
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: Investment in expensive imaging infrastructure for MCI conversion prediction is not supported by evidence when cognitive assessments are available. Imaging adds most value for conversion timeline, not binary conversion prediction.

known_assumptions.belief: Alpha band suppression is the primary EEG marker of MCI
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Classical EEG-MCI literature, 1990s-2010s
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: ML feature importance or graph-metric analysis identifies delta or theta band as the highest-weight EEG discriminator over alpha
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: EEG MCI protocols should prioritise delta/theta connectivity metrics over alpha power suppression depending on the target (amyloid burden vs hippocampal damage).

known_assumptions.belief: Transfer learning from any large medical imaging dataset to MCI improves performance regardless of source domain pathology
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Transfer learning literature applied to medical imaging, 2017-2022
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: Model transferred from a pathologically incompatible source domain performs below a directly trained baseline; or XAI shows transferred attention maps highlight irrelevant anatomical regions
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: Source domain biological compatibility must be verified before transfer learning. Domain-compatibility checks require systematic cross-paper analysis of source domain pathological focus vs target domain requirements.

known_assumptions.belief: Hippocampal texture features carry independent discriminative information beyond hippocampal volume for MCI detection
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Radiomics MCI literature, 2018-2023
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: Radiomics texture features from hippocampus achieve accuracy convergent with FreeSurfer volumetric features on the same task and dataset, implying texture adds no independent signal
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: For current-state MCI vs HC classification, hippocampal volume is the primary signal; texture may be more informative for conversion prediction where volumetric differences are smaller.

known_assumptions.belief: The hippocampus (medial temporal lobe) is the most informative single brain region for structural-MRI detection of MCI and for predicting progression from normal cognition to MCI.
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Corpus prior implied by the invalidated-assumption records listed in currently_invalidated_by (audit 2026-08-29)
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: A model or study in which non-hippocampal regions/measures (amygdala subfields, subcortical/white-matter indices, textural or network features) match or beat hippocampal volume for MCI detection or conversion prediction
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: See the linked IA records' clinical_implication fields.

corpus_attestation_2026_09_27.IA-34: Attested in a narrowed form, carried mainly by P-177; the other quotes are supporting only (practice-level or AD-diagnosis statements). PRIMARY: P-177 (C:/Users/aryas/Downloads/PAPERINGO/downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/PMID_33749642_nihms-1843971.pdf, abstract): 'We previously described that among baseline FDG-PET and MRI measures known to be preferentially affected in the preclinical and clinical stages of AD, hippocampal volume was the best predictor of incident MCI within 2 years (79% sensitivity/78% specificity)'. Its summary block frames the study as an attempt 'to improve short-horizon progression prediction beyond standard hippocampal volume metrics', i.e. hippocampal volume is the benchmark to beat. SUPPORTING: P-66 (.../1-s2.0-S0899707124002316-main.pdf, section 2.5): 'the most informative features of the brain images for Alzheimer diagnosis are texture and shape of hippocampus and amygdala regions' (AD diagnosis and two regions, so it supports the hippocampal-radiomics feature family, not single-region primacy for MCI). P-595 (PDF introduction): 'hippocampal volumetry has emerged as a robust MRI biomarker for AD diagnosis', and (discussion) 'Hippocampal atrophy is a significant hallmark of AD neurodegeneration, is widely used in research and clinical diagnosis'. P-581 (PDF): hippocampal volume 'is commonly used in research, trials, and clinical practice'. P-182 (PDF introduction): 'The most widely studied target in AD is the hippocampus (Jack et al. 1992; Fox et al. 1996), and indeed, multiple studies have reported hippocampal volume loss in MCI relative to controls'. These last four describe standard practice rather than a comparative belief and would not attest the prior on their own. NOT attested, and dropped: KA-12's registered 'sufficient ... other regions and measures add little', and the record's 'cerebellum (traditionally viewed as motor-only)' clause, which P-570 itself states only as superseded ('Traditionally associated with motor control, the cerebellum is now recognized for its critical involvement in cognitive processes'). Contrary statements in the corpus show the primacy view is held but contested, which fits a bounded, not refuted, outcome: P-50 (multi-region atrophy); P-581 ('it has limitations regarding the progression from MCI to AD'); P-595 ('in early AD, MTL atrophy is often subtle and not reliably detected by conventional MTA ratings'). Search: the challenger's own regex sweep of summaries.md (hippocampal/medial temporal within 160 characters of most widely/commonly/established/validated/sensitive/informative/reliable/used, best, gold standard, strongest, primary marker, earliest, first affected, well established, reference standard, most studied; 49 hits, P-369 excluded as a known fabricated block), plus the auditor's PDF list; own PyPDF2 extraction of P-570, P-224, P-50, P-99, P-177, P-66, P-182, P-595, P-581 and P-672.

corpus_attestation_2026_09_27.IA-15: P-37 (Bae et al. 2021, Neurobiology of Aging; PDF downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S0197458020304140-main.pdf, Introduction; the challenger re-extracted it and found the text verbatim): "previous research has relied on specific features (e.g., cortical thickness and hippocampal volume) extracted from raw data to train the model (Zheng and Casari, 2018). This approach assumes that the chosen feature is the most informative and may neglect important information inherent in the raw data. CNN is a deep-learning approach that has evolved in recent years to produce better classification performance and feature visualization than conventional machine learning methods across several fields (Borji et al., 2019). A CNN trained on raw, whole brain data can automatically extract the important imaging features and can offer insights beyond current methods in predicting disease progression." This is a belief held in the field (cited to Borji 2019), not P-274's own hypothesis. Supporting, from P-274's own Discussion (verbatim): "in the study by [22], they received significantly better results using a DL model and MRI images compared to e.g. MMSE, hippocampal volume, cerebrospinal fluid Aβ and tau". The block phrase "Many studies assume deep imaging models are superior", quoted by the 2026-09-15 second reader, was written by the summariser and does not appear in the P-274 PDF. Attestation therefore rests on P-37.
corpus_attestation_2026_09_27.IA-16: P-344 (Jahani et al. 2025, BMC Med Res Methodol 25:250; PDF downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/PMID_41193962_12874_2025_Article_2689.pdf); the challenger re-extracted it and found the text verbatim. Introduction: "Machine learning survival methods have gained attention for their ability to model nonlinear relationships without traditional assumptions [6, 17]. Gradient Boosting Survival Analysis (GBSA) [18] and RSF [19] have shown superior performance over classical Cox regression in biomedical datasets [20, 21]." Discussion: "Sarica et al. [25] compared tree-based survival models, including RSF, with the CoxPH model for predicting the conversion from MCI to AD, revealing that ..." and "These studies consistently highlight RSF as a superior model in predicting dementia-related outcomes." P-309 Introduction (verbatim): "the traditional Cox model may be unstable and inaccurate. Machine learning and deep learning are characterized by the ability to address nonlinearity, strongly correlated variables and accurate predictions." P-344's abstract also calls the question open ("their application in MCI-to-AD progression prediction remains limited, with unclear superiority over classical survival models"). The prior is therefore held but contested; it is still attested for MCI-to-AD prediction.
corpus_attestation_2026_09_27.IA-40: P-79 (Wu et al. 2026, Expert Systems with Applications, an MCI-detection study; PDF downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S0957417425046184-main.pdf, Introduction; the challenger found the text verbatim): "most existing DFCN-based approaches primarily focus on cross-window temporal dynamics while modeling only pairwise relationships between regions of interest (ROIs) within each window. Such approaches disregard how inter-regional function extends beyond simple pairwise interactions, with high-order cooperation among multiple brain regions often reflecting more informative pathological patterns. Moreover, functional connectivity matrices constructed purely from correlation or mutual information neglect high-order topological structures and network hierarchies within each window, potentially limiting both diagnostic accuracy and biomarker discovery." P-516's own Introduction attributes the correlation's-correlation belief to earlier work (verbatim): "the two sequential PCs (denoted as PC2 in this paper) provide a high-order statistic that, in theory, can encode more complex relationship ... Chen et al. (2016) revealed that PC2 can encode the complex interactions between different ROIs, and Zhang et al. (2016) found that PC2 is more sensitive to AD identification." Limits: P-79 builds its high-order networks by regression (NRR), not by correlation's correlation, and no corpus study other than P-516 itself mentions PC2. The belief that raising the order of PCn beyond n=2 helps is NOT attested: it is P-516's own research question ("what will happen if continuing the correlation operation to construct much higher-order BFN by PCn(n>2)").

corpus_attestation_2026_09_27.IA-27: Attested (SFCT half only). P-830 (Ge et al. 2021, Ageing Research Reviews systematic review and meta-analysis), PDF abstract (extract glyphs decoded: 'D' = '<', invisible glyph = '='): 'Compared with healthy controls, patients with MCI also had lower thickness of pRNFL (SMD -0.324, p < 0.001), total macular (SMD -0.302, p < 0.001), and subfoveal choroid (SMD -0.462, p = 0.020).' Discussion: 'The thinner retina and choroid, reduced complexity of vessels, and reduced blood flow were consistently detected in the MCI stage compared with healthy controls' (Table 1, MCI choroidal thickness: OCT k = 4, n = 427, limitation codes a, c, d). Also P-363's own introduction (PDF pp. 359-360): 'A recent meta-analysis found that SFCT was significantly decreased in patients with AD compared with that of control subjects. ... SFCT was also shown to decrease in subjects with mild cognitive impairment (MCI)'; and P-1317 (Joseph et al. 2024; PDF at downloads/3. Molecular, Genetic and Fluid Biomarkers/1-s2.0-S2666914524000162-main.pdf, which is missing from data/paper_pdf_map.json): 'Other studies analyzing the choroid have reported decreased subfoveal choroidal thickness in both MCI [35: Bulut et al. 2016] and AD when compared with that of controls.' The registered prior KA-20 as written ('Retinal/choroidal markers change in a fixed direction with MCI: the choroid thins (SFCT) and retinal vessels become more tortuous') is NOT attested: its assumed_since reads 'Corpus prior implied by the invalidated-assumption records listed in currently_invalidated_by', so it was built from IA-27 and IA-46 themselves, and no corpus study states its tortuosity half. CHALLENGER ADDITION: P-830 is not fully independent of the disproving cohort. Its reference list contains 'Robbins, C.B., Grewal, D.S., Thompson, A.C., Powers, J.H., Soundararajan, S., Koo, H.Y., Yoon, S.P., Polascik, B.W., Liu, A., Agrawal, R., Fekrat, S., 2020. Choroidal structural analysis in alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, and cognitively healthy controls. Am. J. Ophthalmol.' (= P-363). Its MCI Table 1 row 'Choroidal angioarchitecture OCTA (k 1, n 204) ... Greater total choroidal area and luminal area, lower choroidal vascularity index' reports P-363's findings, and its text reads 'thinning of the choroid via OCTA (Robbins et al., 2020) ... The thinning of the choroid could also be detected in MCI'. So P-363 was among P-830's included studies and may sit in the k = 4 SFCT pool. P-830 still attests that the field holds the prior, and the P-363 introduction and P-1317 state it independently. But P-830 is not an independent counterweight to P-363.

corpus_attestation_2026_09_27.IA-35: Attested. In its general form the prior is stated by the disproving study itself (P-144, the canonical ID of the Vergani 2025 paper; P-576 is its dedup stub). From the Conclusion of PDF downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S2213158225000300-main.pdf: 'ERP dynamics, in particular, revealed critical discontinuities in cognitive decline, challenging the assumption of a linear progression from health to pathology. These deviations could reflect compensatory mechanisms and cerebral resilience, disrupting expected ERP monotonicity. Our methodology captures these nonlinear changes, offering insights beyond standard markers like amplitude attenuation or latency slowing'. Fig. 1E caption: 'Dashed line traces the hypothetical monotonic trend which has been altered by the features values.' An independent corpus study instantiates the monotonic expectation for P3: P-489 (PDF 1-s2.0-S2405844023028487-main.pdf) reports 'there was a gradual decrease in the amplitude and increase in the latency of the P3 potential from the HC group to the AD group'. P-28 treats P300 as a progression marker: 'N200 and P300 latency have been considered as promising biomarkers in the early diagnosis and progression assessment of AD and MCI'. So the prior is not a strawman, but the only corpus statement of it for all components is the disproving study's own framing, which the master already discloses for most priors ('most were registered from the contradicting records themselves').

corpus_attestation_2026_09_27.IA-67: Primary (added by challenger): the P-249 PDF itself, Discussion, reporting what the field's earlier syntheses concluded rather than its own hypothesis: 'Our findings are only partly consistent with previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses that recognized a moderate and clinically relevant effect of physical exercise interventions on the cognitive function of older adults (De Souto Barreto et al., 2018; Gallardo-Gomez et al., 2022; Northey et al., 2018).' Its Introduction records that the belief is contested: 'A recent umbrella review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) has cast doubt on the cognitive benefits of physical exercise interventions' and 'meta-analyses have failed to consistently corroborate the hypothesis that exercise interventions can effectively mitigate the risk of clinically meaningful cognitive deterioration, MCI, or the advent of dementia'. Independent corpus source: P-680 PDF (downloads/1. Clinical Assessments, Behavioral and Social Factors/1-s2.0-S0167494324002176-main.pdf), Introduction: 'Exercise is considered among the most effective nonpharmacological strategies to prevent cognitive decline in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and prevent dementia in further stages of MCI (Petersen et al., 2018).' The record's lead anchor P-251 cannot be used. data/paper_pdf_map.json maps it to downloads/4. Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S001048252401388X-main.pdf, and a fresh extract of that file is 'Plasma protein-based identification of neuroimage-driven subtypes in mild cognitive impairment via protein-protein interaction aware explainable graph propagational network' (Park et al., doi 10.1016/j.compbiomed.2024.109303; the same file is also mapped to P-10). The quote therefore reconciles with no corpus source. P-806 shares authors with P-249 (NI-10). The belief is attested but contested, so 'robust, established ... stated as settled' overstates it.

Computational Models and Modern AI Architectures/1-s2.0-S1746809420303773-main.pdf; data/paper_pdf_map.json doi 10.1016/j.bspc.2020.102249) is Ghoraani et al. 2021, 'Detection of mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease using dual-task gait assessments and machine learning', BSPC 64:102249 - a gait paper, not an EEG paper. IA-11's summary_match was checked against the block, not the literature, so the disproof_signal here rests on a block whose bibliographic identity is unverified (the EEG study it describes is unidentified in the corpus). Do not treat KA-33 as a registered, evidenced invalidation until P-112 is re-attached to its real paper or the EEG block is assigned to a verified P-ID. Status left as proposed_2026_09_09; IA-11 not touched (outside this package - see handoff).

known_assumptions.domain: Trial endpoint adjudication (MCI due to AD)
known_assumptions.belief: Investigator-only endpoint ascertainment does not miss clinically adjudicated MCI-due-to-AD events, so endpoint adjudication in an AD prevention trial can be confined to cases the site investigator has flagged as having reached MCI due to AD.
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Phase-3 AD prevention trial design practice (TOMMORROW adopted MCI due to AD as a primary endpoint event; corpus prior confirmed by IA-101; operator G5 2026-09-10)
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: P-866 (TOMMORROW adjudication record, 648 dossiers / 386 participants / 96 events): blinded three-stage committee agreed with investigator determinations only 71.0% (kappa 0.327 for MCI due to AD); on the two-consecutive-visit safeguard subset agreement FELL to 40.5% by end of study; 41/410 investigator-negative cases declared events = 42.7% of all 96 - 'events that would have been missed if the adjudications had been limited only to cases when the investigator felt an endpoint had been reached'.
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: Prevention trials cannot rely on investigator-only endpoint ascertainment for MCI-due-to-AD; independent adjudication of investigator-negative cases is required to avoid missing roughly 40% of events.
known_assumptions.provenance: Registered by the operator G5 pass 2026-09-10 (human gate; coordinator-written event logs/gate_events.log) after PDF-provenance verification of P-866. KA scoped per consolidated verdict to 'investigator-only endpoint ascertainment can miss clinically adjudicated MCI-due-to-AD events' - NOT 'the MCI-due-to-AD construct is unreliable'.
known_assumptions.belief_before_audit_2026_09_14: The transition to MCI due to AD is a determinate clinical fact that a trained investigator can be relied on to recognise, so investigator-only endpoint ascertainment is a dependable basis for registration-trial endpoints.
known_assumptions.audit_note_2026_09_14: 2026-09-14 audit (IA package): belief rewritten from the construct-level wording ('The transition to MCI due to AD is a determinate clinical fact that a trained investigator can be relied on to recognise ...') to the narrow ascertainment wording the operator's own 2026-09-10 G5 verdict required (see provenance: 'investigator-only endpoint ascertainment can miss clinically adjudicated MCI-due-to-AD events' - NOT 'the MCI-due-to-AD construct is unreliable'). Support: summaries.md P-866 block L132008 'Among the 410 cases where investigator diagnoses did not support an endpoint, the committee disagreed in 41 (10%) and declared an event - and those 41 represent 42.7% of all 96 events in the trial ... "These are events that would have been missed if the adjudications had been limited only to cases when the investigator felt an endpoint had been reached."'; L132044 construct reliability 'raise[d] without settling'. disproof_signal and clinical_implication_if_disproved already narrow - unchanged. Matching edit applied to IA-101 what_disproved_it / prior_belief. Status unchanged (operator gate).

known_assumptions.belief: Polypharmacy medication count is a risk marker for MCI-to-dementia progression whose presence raises expected cognitive decline (the harm direction of the prior literature).
known_assumptions.assumed_since: P-827 ('the adverse impact of polypharmacy on cognitive function', anchored to a 2024 systematic review), P-1012 ('Polypharmacy has been linked to cognitive decline'), P-970 (risk-factor list); corpus prior confirmed by IA-102; operator G5 2026-09-10
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: P-1157 (237 Taiwanese MCI, median 34 mo, annual CDR): adjusted HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.31-0.78) for progression with polypharmacy (>=5 prescriptions), KM p=0.005, 89/237 events; corroborated by P-1012 protective profiles OR 0.421 (0.232-0.762, p=0.004) / OR 0.278 (0.137-0.565, p<0.001). The harm direction does not reproduce at the MCI-to-dementia transition.
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: Medication count is not a directionally stable risk marker for MCI-to-dementia progression; the harm direction fails at this stage. Marker-level claim only - confounding by indication (care intensity/ascertainment) is a competing explanation for the protective sign, so no causal reading is licensed.
known_assumptions.provenance: Registered by the operator G5 pass 2026-09-10 (human gate; coordinator-written event logs/gate_events.log) after PDF-provenance verification of P-1157/P-1012. KA re-scoped per consolidated verdict to marker-level, transition-specific wording; causal reading affirmatively barred.

known_assumptions.domain: Non-pharmacological intervention trials in MCI (non-specific / placebo effects)
known_assumptions.belief: The apparent cognitive benefit reported by non-pharmacological training trials in MCI is driven by non-specific expectancy, engagement, motivation and novelty rather than by the trained content itself.
known_assumptions.assumed_since: Sourced from three corpus papers INDEPENDENTLY of any invalidated-assumption record. (1) P-859's own Introduction states the objection as field-held: summaries.md L130638 'A standing objection to the whole cognitive-training literature is that its effects are driven by expectancy, engagement, motivation and novelty rather than by training'; the same clause is in the source PDF, pdf_extract_859.txt L9, 'there are concerns that CCT's effects are driven by factors such as expectancy, engagement, motivation, and novelty (3, 4)', citing external references 3-4. (2) P-759, an MCI acupuncture meta-analysis, applies the belief as an operative judgement: summaries.md L73813 'the primary outcomes are examiner-administered scales, so the entire efficacy signal is currently confounded with assessor and participant expectancy'. (3) P-700, a VR-training study in MCI, applies it in a different intervention family: summaries.md L62895 'expectancy and attention effects are not separable from any specific effect of the virtual environment'.
known_assumptions.disproof_signal: A randomised MCI trial in which measured pre-randomisation expectancy dissociates from outcome - in particular an arm patients expected LESS from outperforming the arm they expected MORE from - or in which measured expectancy predicts no change in the primary cognitive outcome. Note the four constructs are not interchangeable: a test of expectancy alone leaves engagement, motivation and novelty unaddressed.
known_assumptions.clinical_implication_if_disproved: See the linked IA record's clinical_implication field. Broadly: an active-control training trial's benefit could not be discounted as a pure non-specific artefact on the strength of the standing objection alone, and downgrades applied to unblinded MCI intervention evidence on expectancy grounds (e.g. P-759, P-700) would need to be re-argued rather than assumed.
known_assumptions.provenance: Minted 2026-09-14 on operator instruction (IA package item 3a) so that IA-103 has a registered prior to point at instead of the placeholder 'NEW_KA_PROPOSED'. PROPOSED, NOT CONFIRMED: registering the prior does not gate IA-103, whose status remains candidate_pending_human_review with an unapplied scope narrowing and an unreconciled load-bearing statistic (see IA-103.scope_operator_review_2026_09_14 and .blocker_operator_review_2026_09_14). No operator gate is claimed by this entry.
known_assumptions.no_circularity_sourcing_2026_09_14: The belief text is taken from P-859's Introduction and from the operational applications in P-759 and P-700. It is NOT derived from IA-103, and IA-103 is not cited in assumed_since as the source of the prior. This is deliberate: KA-50's assumed_since cites only the IA record that is said to invalidate it ('corpus prior confirmed by IA-NEW-1110-01'), a circular sourcing pattern flagged at the 2026-09-14 audit, and KA-53 must not repeat it. currently_invalidated_by lists IA-103 as the claiming record only - the same convention as KA-24/25/26, which list un-gated IA records - and confers no status on it.
known_assumptions.caveat_2026_09_14: P-859 itself records that the empirical expectancy literature in this field 'is sparse, with mixed findings, and has been restricted to cognitively intact adults', so this prior is a widely-voiced methodological objection rather than a settled empirical finding; an operator may reasonably judge it closer to equipoise than to a field-held positive claim. Vocabulary note: assumption_type 'Mechanism_Reframing' is not in the file's own assumption_types enum (six values, none of them this), but is the established in-file value used by KA-24 and is the category IA-103's proposed registry text names.
known_assumptions.operator_review_2026_09_14: Minted by the assistant on operator instruction 2026-09-14 (IA package item 3a): register the expectancy prior covering all four constructs, sourced non-circularly. Status proposed; no gate implied or claimed.
